overview: Typhoid fever is a life-threatening infection caused by the bacterium Salmonella Typhi, usually spread through contaminated food or water, and can lead to serious complications or death if left untreated. Urbanization and climate change may increase the global burden of typhoid, and antibiotic resistance is a growing concern. Improved living conditions and antibiotics have reduced typhoid fever in industrialized countries, but it remains a public health problem in many developing areas.
prevention: Injectable vaccine based on purified antigen
risk_factors: Lack of access to safe water
key_facts: 9 million cases of typhoid fever annually
Two typhoid conjugate vaccines have been prequalified by WHO since December 2017
